title: A Oath for the Salt
premise: Paloma Galloway has hidden her swordspeaker's gift for twenty years, selling charms and keeping her oaths unspoken, until the crown's new witch-hunt forces her to flee the city with a stolen registry of every gifted person in the realm. Gathering a ragtag company of the hunted—a disgraced inquisitor's daughter, a mute boy whose silence is itself a spell, and the soldier sent to kill her who chooses otherwise—she searches for the Salt Door, the last passage out of a country that erased its own magic and, with it, its own history. The door can only be opened by an oath spoken aloud, the very act that will reveal her and doom everyone she loves. In the end Paloma speaks her oath, holds the hunt at bay long enough for the others to pass through, and stays behind to become the door itself—found family scattered to freedom, her identity finally claimed at the cost of her old life.
about_author: Emrys Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing outlawed folk charms in coastal libraries before turning to fiction. They write about borders, oaths, and the people countries try to forget.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the port city of Brackwater, Paloma sells a luck-knot to a fisherman's widow, concealing her gift behind mundane craft. When a crier proclaims the crown's Edict of Ash—every gifted person to be registered or burned—her oldest customer is dragged into the square. The beat: the fragile peace of her double life shatters.

chapters.title: The Registry
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma breaks into the magistrate's hall to steal the registry naming every gifted soul in the realm, including children she once taught. She escapes with the book but is seen by a soldier, Sergeant Ivo Ren, who hesitates a heartbeat too long before raising the alarm. The beat: guilt and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reports the theft but lies about the thief's face, haunted by the memory of Paloma binding his brother's dying wound with a spoken oath years ago. He begins quietly sabotaging the hunt. The beat: a hunter's first act of mercy.

chapters.title: The Mute Boy
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Fleeing Brackwater, Paloma finds Tam, a mute orphan whose silence literally unmakes sound around him—a gift the edict would burn. He clings to her; she swears she won't leave him. The beat: the found family begins with one small, desperate bond.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, rendered through his drawings and gestures. The pair travels the old salt road, where Tam's gift reveals echoes of the country's erased magical past. Paloma realizes the realm didn't lose its magic—it buried it deliberately. The beat: wonder shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a river town, they're cornered by hunt-captain Serah Vane—who recognizes the registry's worth and, to Paloma's shock, offers to help. Her father wrote the edict; she wants to undo him. The beat: distrust offered a fragile hand.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah reveals the legend of the Salt Door, the last gate out of the realm, sealed when the old kingdom dissolved. Only a spoken oath of the swordspeaker line can open it. Paloma admits what she is for the first time in twenty years. The beat: identity spoken aloud, terrifying and liberating.

chapters.title: The Soldier's Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo is caught sabotaging the hunt and branded a traitor; he kills his former commander in self-defense and goes on the run. The beat: no way back.

chapters.title: Four at the Fire
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The fugitives unite—Paloma, Tam, Serah, and a wounded Ivo—sharing a meal in a ruined chapel. Old grievances surface: Serah burned a charm-seller once; Ivo hunted Paloma's kind. The beat: forgiveness argued for, not yet granted.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah's father, Inquisitor Vane, deduces her betrayal and sets a trap using her mother as bait. The company must decide whether to walk into it. The beat: love tested against survival.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At a mass grave of the first purged swordspeakers, Paloma performs the rites she's avoided for two decades, and the dead's echoes show her the Salt Door's true location—beneath the drowned cathedral at Greyharbor. The beat: grief transformed into direction.

chapters.title: The Bait
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The rescue of Serah's mother goes wrong; Vane expected them. Ivo takes a crossbow bolt meant for Tam. They escape with the mother but lose their supplies and their lead on the hunters. The beat: costly, imperfect victory.

chapters.title: Fever and Oaths
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, delirious. Ivo dreams of his brother and of Paloma's old oath over him. Waking, he confesses he was the soldier who saw her at the magistrate's hall. The beat: honesty as the price of belonging.

chapters.title: The Drowned City
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The company reaches half-sunken Greyharbor, where Tam's silence-gift quiets the treacherous tides long enough to guide them through flooded streets to the cathedral spire. The beat: the smallest member becomes their anchor.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Inquisitor Vane corners them at the cathedral, offering Paloma a deal: her public surrender and execution in exchange for amnesty for every name in the registry. The beat: an impossible arithmetic of one life against hundreds.

chapters.title: The Door Below
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Beneath the cathedral, they find the Salt Door—vast, brined, and waiting—but it demands an oath spoken in the old tongue, which will announce Paloma's location to every hunter in the realm. The beat: the trap inside the escape.

chapters.title: A Mother's Testimony
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Serah's mother testifies publicly that the purges were built on forged evidence, buying the company one day of chaos as the city turns on the inquisition. The beat: justice outside the law, won with words instead of swords.

chapters.title: The Oath for the Salt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vane breaks the truce and attacks at the Door. Paloma speaks her full oath—naming herself, her dead teachers, her found family—and the Door opens in a tide of light as the battle rages. The beat: the climax; identity as weapon and key.

chapters.title: Who Stays
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Door will hold open only while a swordspeaker's oath sustains it. Paloma chooses to stay. Ivo, Serah, Tam, and Serah's mother pass through, each goodbye a small wound. Tam presses his silence-gift into her palm like a stone. The beat: heartbreak chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Door Itself
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Alone with Vane's last soldiers, Paloma holds the Door against the hunt, her gift transfiguring her into something part-stone, part-tide, part-story. She defeats Vane not by killing him but by binding him with an oath of witness—he will remember, and tell, forever. The beat: victory as transformation.

chapters.title: The Country That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Serah's POV, beyond the Door. The refugees emerge into a coastline of scattered settlements where the exiled gifted built lives. Serah begins teaching the old tongue; Ivo plants Paloma's luck-knots in harbor soil. The beat: mourning braided with hope.

chapters.title: Luck for the Living
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. Years later, travelers tell of a door of salt that opens for those who speak true names, guarded by a woman who remembers everyone. Tam, now grown, returns through it to sit with her. The beat: found family enduring across the threshold; identity as a gift given away and returned.
